messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate highways: 70 mph (except 55 mph on I‑35).
• Urban interstate highways: 65 mph.
• Residential streets: 25 mph (unless posted otherwise). | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on the right. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Do not pass on the left unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or intersection.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited. | | **School Bus Laws** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Towed vehicles must have a valid registration and license plate. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras enforce speed limits; violations result in fines. | | **Roadside Assistance & Emergency Services** | • 911 for emergencies; 1‑800‑TRUCK‑HELP for towing. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 1) – full statutory text. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) website – regulations, forms, and updates. - Texas Highway Patrol – enforcement guidelines and public safety notices. **Common Enforcement Practices** - Police may issue citations for speeding, seat‑belt violations, DUI, and cell‑phone use. - Fines vary by offense and location; repeat offenders face higher penalties. - Courts may impose mandatory education courses or license suspensions. **Recent Updates (2024)** - New “no‑handheld” phone law effective 2024‑01‑01. - Updated speed limit on I‑35 to 55 mph in rural sections. - Expanded use of automated traffic enforcement cameras in major cities. Feel free to let me know if you need more specific details, such as how to appeal a ticket, or if you’re interested in recent court cases related to Texas traffic laws.
